- Request and justification: Raphael requested a bounded regression probe of the already-pinned @fission-ai/openspec@1.16.0 Claude core profile. Existing repository coverage exercises metadata/task/archive interoperability but not the generated core workflow inventory and absence of optional-workflow handoffs. - Scope and exclusions: The sole product edit is tests/openspec-cli-compatibility.mjs, plus this change's native planning artifacts. Assert six generated core skills and command inventory, scan all generated Claude skill/command files for omitted optional-workflow spellings, and exercise synthetic negative/isolation controls. No README/docs/config/manifests/skills/scripts/other-test edits, installed-profile writes, upstream upgrades, schema adoption, migration, or general installer.
- Expected outcome and acceptance boundary: Independently reviewed test-only source integration with actual focused and repository gate evidence, followed by separately authorized integrated verification and normal factual closure. No dependency on unmerged parallel-change-workflow candidate A (552382f2756703e7b57cb24d8088773d1e1aed51; https://github.com/forgegod/ai-coding-agent-skills/issues/8). Fresh merge-base/path and semantic review found the bounded probe scope independent. The Lossless draft remains sequenced behind A and is not a B prerequisite.

## Impact and estimated blast radius
- Affected components, environments and people: Opt-in local compatibility probe and disposable scratch fixtures; maintainers invoking npm run test:openspec. No deployed application or package payload changes.
- Data and trust boundaries: Future execution downloads the exact public npm package under the existing credential-minimal environment; HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, npm cache, and generated Claude files stay in scratch. This is isolation against accidental inheritance, not an OS sandbox or package-integrity guarantee.
- Worst credible failure and blast radius: A weak inventory/reference assertion gives false compatibility confidence; a bad fixture boundary reads host configuration or writes outside scratch; upstream/network failures block the opt-in gate. No real profile is an input or output.
- Assumptions and unknowns: Pinned upstream source defines six core workflows and existing handoff filtering, but this new fixture has not been executed. Actual generated-file evidence and all implementation results remain pending. No change to the project's seven-workflow installation requirement is intended.

## Risk assessment and treatment
- Confidentiality: Low qualitative estimate with scratch HOME/config and explicit environment allowlist; npm package execution still trusts upstream code and PATH. Never retain secrets.
- Integrity: Low-to-medium qualitative estimate: false-negative reference matching is the main risk. Exact inventories, non-vacuous recursive scanning, per-spelling synthetic negative controls, and independent exact-candidate review mitigate it.
- Availability: Low; npm/network unavailability fails the opt-in probe, not a production service. Preserve raw failure output.
- Likelihood and risk: No numeric project risk method identified; these are agent estimates, not operator risk acceptance.
- Mitigations and residual risk: Keep the exact pin and existing npm-exec flags, retain command/status/stdout/stderr and fixture inventory, remove scratch home/cache in finally on success or failure, preserve existing metadata/archive coverage, and stop rather than widen the one-file scope. An allowlisted environment is not a security sandbox.
- Applicable policy / SoA: Root AGENTS.md, selected OpenSpec SDLC, identity-only metadata and proposal-time issue policy; no SoA applicability or ISO/IEC 27001 conformity claim is established.

## Verification and recovery plan
- Verification: After separate execution authorization, npm run test:openspec is the focused gate. Require npm test, npm run build, npm run validate:openspec, strict native OpenSpec validation and whitespace checks after the final edit. Exact six-skill and six-command inventories, every omitted optional spelling, environment isolation and synthetic dangling-reference rejection are acceptance evidence. No implementation/release gates run during this proposal. Scanner/native installer release probes are not required by this test-only non-package delta; reassess on scope change rather than silently expand.
- Rollout and abort conditions: Local reviewed test change only, then separately authorized protected publication/integration. Stop for overlapping active scope, any extra required product path, failed gate, environment/profile leak, or unresolved review finding.
- Recovery: Preserve raw failure logs and fixtures; repair the test in the same bounded change under renewed authority or revert the test-only change by normal reviewed Git procedure. Never reset another workspace or modify a user profile.
- Communication: Present this issue, local artifact locations, overlap verdict and explicit pending freeze/approval boundary to Raphael. Later implementation/review/publication outcomes need their own authority and factual evidence.

## Ownership and authorization boundary
- Requester and accountable operator: Raphael, invoking repository operator; no automatic assignee or execution lock.
- Risk owner / required approvers: Raphael for scope and exact immutable plan approval; an independent exact-candidate reviewer is required before later integration. Risk acceptance and plan approval remain pending.
- Authorization: The ***'s explicit planning-only openspec-propose request authorizes one generated identity, automatic isolated proposal workspace, native artifacts, this policy-required issue/readback, native planning validation, and operator-guide recording. It prohibits implementation, commits/plan freeze, profile writes, publication, pull requests, CI dispatch, merge/archive/finish, and Later D.
- Reassessment triggers: Any additional product path, change to pin/prerequisites/install policy, altered sibling scope, environment or data boundary, candidate revision, rollout or gate requirements.
